name: Typical asking rent
definition: Zillow Observed Rent Index for New York City: the typical asking rent for homes and apartments listed for rent, all homes plus multifamily, smoothed, annual average of monthly values, in current dollars.

source.name: Zillow Research, Zillow Observed Rent Index (ZORI), city level, all homes plus multifamily, smoothed, monthly (City_zori_uc_sfrcondomfr_sm_month.csv)

peers.note: Zillow city regions matched on RegionName plus State. Nashville-Davidson is Zillow's "Nashville, TN" and Washington, D.C. is Zillow's "Washington, DC"; Zillow's city boundaries are its own and may not match Census place boundaries exactly.

method: Annual value = mean of the 12 monthly ZORI values for the calendar year (Zillow labels each month by its last day), rounded to whole dollars. Not adjusted for inflation. Where Zillow leaves a month blank, the year is the mean of the months it published (listed in caveats); no month is filled in. Peer 2025 values require all 12 months.
caveats: Measures asking rents on units listed for rent, not what sitting tenants pay, so it moves faster than rents across the whole housing stock (including rent-stabilized leases).
Zillow revises past values when it updates the index, so earlier years can change between downloads.
In current dollars: some of the rise over time is general inflation.
Months Zillow leaves blank in the New York series, averaged over the remaining months of that year rather than filled in: New York, NY: blank 2020-09.
